question: Is rereading your notes a good way to prepare for a test?
keyIdea: Your answer has the key idea: rereading feels familiar but doesn't show what you recall.
model: Not on its own. Rereading feels familiar but doesn't show what you can recall. Close your notes and test yourself, spaced out over several days.
unsureKeyIdea: You may have the key idea. Compare with the model answer.
noMatch: Your answer doesn't match the key idea or a common misconception. Compare with the model answer.

misconceptions.label: Rereading builds memory
misconceptions.why: Familiarity can feel like knowing, so test your recall over several days instead.

misconceptions.label: Highlighting is studying
misconceptions.why: Marking words doesn't show what you recall, so close your notes and test yourself.

misconceptions.label: Cramming the night before works as well
misconceptions.idea: cramming works as well as spaced practice
misconceptions.why: Cramming fades faster, so spread your self-tests over several days.

misconceptions.label: Some people only learn by watching
misconceptions.idea: some people can learn only by watching
misconceptions.why: A preference isn't a fixed learning style, so practise recalling what you watched.
